subject: SIG initiation: form selection, encryption boundary, and SOC 2 timing
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@clearskyhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: SIG initiation: form selection, encryption boundary, and SOC 2 timing

Hi Tom —

Thanks again for taking time this morning. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying asks so we can kick the security intake forward cleanly: 

What we heard
- You want to move forward with a security questionnaire as the next step (good).
- Primary concerns: data residency in US, encryption at rest, and fine-grained RBAC for clinical users.

Asks / decisions needed from Clearsky
1) SOC 2 status: do you have a completed SOC 2 Type II report, or is one in flight? If in flight, an expected completion quarter is helpful.
2) Preferred questionnaire: SIG (full), CAIQ, or a custom vendor form? We can accept any but have a slightly faster path for CAIQ-prefill.
3) Encryption boundary: do you use customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for sensitive fields, or is encryption provider-managed? Any short bullet answer will do.
4) Attachments: if you have a network diagram or existing questionnaire, please attach.

Timeline: if you can get answers back by end of week we can prefill and route to our security team for evidence review (target 3 business days after prefill).

Next steps from our side
- Ben will be the technical lead for evidence requests.
- Jordan will coordinate contract/procurement timeline if we need an SLA exception.

Thanks — short bullets are perfect. I’ll consolidate and send the CAIQ template if you prefer that path.

Mina Haddad
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com
(415) 555-0123

Attachments: (none)
From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@clearskyhealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Kapoor <aisha.kapoor@clearskyhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 13:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: SIG initiation: form selection, encryption boundary, and SOC 2 timing

Mina —

Thanks for the clear recap. Short answers below, followed by a couple of follow-ups: 

1) SOC 2: We do not yet have a Type II. We completed a SOC 2 Type I in Nov 2025 and kicked off Type II testing this month; our auditor expects finalization by 2026-Q3.

2) Questionnaire: our security team prefers CAIQ because it maps directly to our existing controls matrix, but we can work with SIG-lite if Redwood finds CAIQ harder to consume.

3) Encryption boundary: we use provider-managed disk encryption for most data, but sensitive PHI fields are encrypted with AWS KMS CMKs (customer-managed keys) scoped per-tenant.

4) Attachments: attaching our vendor questionnaire and a simple network diagram (DOCX + PNG).

Questions from us:
- What level of evidence do you typically need for CAIQ answers (screenshots, audit logs, architecture diagram)?
- Who should our security contact expect from Redwood during evidence review?

We’ll plan to have the CAIQ prefills back to you by Tuesday (03/16). If that works, please send the template and any prefill tips.

Best,
Tom Ellis
Head of IT & Security | Clearsky Health
tom.ellis@clearskyhealth.com

Attachments: Clearsky_VENDOR_questionnaire_v1.docx, network-diagram.png
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: SIG initiation: form selection, encryption boundary, and SOC 2 timing

On Wed, Mar 11, 2026 at 9:15 AM Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com> wrote:
> (original message omitted)

Tom — thanks for the quick reply and the attachments. A few clarifications from the Redwood security intake perspective so we can avoid back-and-forth: 

- Evidence expectations: for CAIQ we generally ask for a mix of configuration screenshots (IAM/KMS policies), a short architecture diagram, and one example of logs or access reviews. We do not require full audit exports in the intake phase — that’s requested later if we need to validate a specific control.

- KMS details: the fact you use CMKs per-tenant is helpful. Can you confirm the KMS is in the same AWS account as the workloads, or is it in a central security account with cross-account access? One line here is enough.

- Network boundary: the diagram is helpful; can you add whether you have any peered customer VPCs or if integration is via API only? This affects the evidence path.

Operational next steps:
1) If you prefer CAIQ, send back a prefilled CAIQ (fine to mark some items as 'in process'); we will review and list evidence owners.
2) If CAIQ is not possible, SIG-lite is acceptable — it may take us a little longer.

Short timeline: if you ship a CAIQ prefill by 03/16, I’ll aim to get back with a prioritized evidence request list by 03/19. My contact info below — I’ll be the primary security reviewer.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0199

Attachments: (none)
From: Aisha Kapoor <aisha.kapoor@clearskyhealth.com>

Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@clearskyhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 16:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: SIG initiation: form selection, encryption boundary, and SOC 2 timing

Ben / Mina —

Thanks — we’ll proceed with CAIQ prefill. A few quick notes now that we’ve reviewed internally: 

- KMS ownership: CMKs live in our central security AWS account and are accessed via cross-account roles by the application account.
- Network: integration is API-only; we do not peer customer VPCs. The attached network-diagram.png has a one-page callout of traffic flows.
- SOC 2: noted (Type II target Q3). We will mark items as 'in progress' where appropriate.

We attached the vendor questionnaire we typically send to partners (Clearsky_VENDOR_questionnaire_v1.docx) and the diagram. Ben — for the evidence bits you mentioned, who should we send screenshots/links to? Prefer a single S3 share or emailed PDFs?

We expect to return the CAIQ prefill by Monday 03/16 and can follow up with artifacts then.

Aisha Kapoor
Security Program Manager | Clearsky Health
aisha.kapoor@clearskyhealth.com
